about: Types of Headaches is a simple medical-style chart titled "Types of Headaches" with four bald, beige heads in profile. Three are real: Migraine, with red on one side of the forehead; Hypertension, with red at the back of the skull; and Stress, with a red band wrapped around the head. The fourth head is entirely red, from crown to chin. That last one gets a new label: the thing that gives you the worst headache imaginable. The joke is the escalation from tidy diagnoses to total full-head agony caused by something annoyingly specific.
origin: The chart started as an illustration for a health article about quick headache relief. Around 2017 people began editing it to add a fourth, completely red head with their own label.
usage:
There is a single text box, placed above the fully red head in the bottom right. Fill it with the most painful, specific annoyance you can think of; the three medical labels set up a pattern that your caption breaks.

The best captions are situations rather than single words: "Breaking Production on a Friday", "Group project with no group", "Reading your own code from 2019". The more precise and relatable the scenario, the more the solid red head feels earned. Keep it short enough to sit over one head, roughly the length of the other three labels plus a few words.
ideas: Group project where you're the only one working
Teammate who won't use voice chat
Explaining the offside rule to relatives
Reading your own code from last year
